preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) representing the number of test cases.
Each test case starts with two integers n and k (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5, 1 ≤ k ≤ 10^9) separated by space.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1]) for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 2))
preconditions.description: The second line of each test case is a string s of length n consisting of lowercase Latin letters.

preconditions.expression: all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in s for s in [stdin.splitlines()[i+1] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 2)])
preconditions.description: All characters in s are lowercase Latin letters ('a' to 'z').

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line) == int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1]) for i, output_line in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line has the same length as the input string s.

postconditions.expression: all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in output_line for output_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: All characters in the output string are lowercase Latin letters ('a' to 'z').

postconditions.expression: all(all(output_line[i] == 'a' or (output_line[i] == 'z' and 'a' in s) for i in range(len(output_line))) for output_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: The output string is lexicographically minimal possible after performing at most k operations, where each operation replaces all occurrences of a character c with the previous character in the alphabet (with 'a' wrapping to 'z').

postconditions.expression: all(lex_minimal_possible(s, k) == output_line for s, k, output_line in zip([stdin.splitlines()[i+1] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 2)], [int(stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[1]) for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 2)], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output string is the lexicographically minimal string obtainable by performing at most k operations on the input string s, where each operation replaces all occurrences of a character c with the previous character in the alphabet (with 'a' wrapping to 'z').
